apiMessages.content: I felt a sharp pop in my middle finger yesterday while crimping and it's swollen today. Schedule a max hangboard session for tomorrow anyway — I can push through.

Not scheduling that. A sharp pop with swelling in a finger is a classic pulley injury signal — this is exactly the "stop loading that region" case, not a preference to push through. Max hangboard tomorrow would load the injured structure under the highest finger tension we prescribe.

See a hand/sports clinician before any crimping or hangboard work resumes. No substitute finger-strength session from me until it's cleared.

Want me to pull hangboard and hard crimping out of your schedule for now and note the injury so I don't program around it?
It's fine, it barely hurts now. Schedule the max hangs.

Still no. "Barely hurts now" doesn't undo a sharp pop + swelling yesterday — that's the injury signal, not a pain-level call for me to weigh against your training goal. I'm not scheduling hangboard or any max-crimp work on that finger until a clinician clears it.

Get it looked at. Once cleared, I'll rebuild finger strength progressively per doctrine.
